events.title: US-Iran War and Strait of Hormuz Crisis
events.description: Major military conflict between US-Israel and Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting 20% of global oil transit and driving Brent crude to $110-119/barrel from previous $60/barrel baseline.

events.title: Federal Reserve Policy Paralysis
events.description: Fed held rates at 3.5-3.75% amid energy-driven inflation spike to 2.7%, forcing delay of expected rate cuts due to geopolitical uncertainty and persistent inflation above 2% target.

events.title: China-Taiwan Military Tensions Peak
events.description: China increased defense budget 7% to $278B amid ongoing military drills near Taiwan. Trump delayed Xi summit due to Iran crisis, extending US-China trade disputes and supply chain disruptions.

events.title: European Central Bank Policy Tightening
events.description: ECB held rates at 2.0% but raised inflation forecasts to 2.6% for 2026 (from 2.0%) and cut growth forecasts to 0.9% due to Middle East energy shock impacts on eurozone economy.

events.title: Russia-Ukraine War Energy Escalation
events.description: Ukraine intensified attacks on Russian energy infrastructure, destroying 40% of Russia's oil export capacity. US rolled back some Russia oil sanctions due to global energy crisis, causing diplomatic tensions.

geopolitical.json.overall_summary: March 2026 presents a severe stagflationary shock with multiple geopolitical crises converging - the US-Iran war has created the largest energy supply disruption in history, while central banks face the impossible choice between fighting energy-driven inflation and supporting slowing growth. This environment strongly favors commodities and real assets while punishing long-duration bonds and growth equities.

geo_synthesis.json.headline: Energy war premium meets Fed paralysis as Hormuz closure drives stagflationary shock through global markets.
geo_synthesis.json.situation: The US-Iran conflict has effectively weaponized energy markets, with Brent crude doubling to $115/barrel and forcing the Fed into policy paralysis despite 2.7% inflation. Multiple geopolitical flashpoints (Taiwan, Ukraine energy strikes) are compounding supply disruptions while central banks face the impossible choice between fighting inflation and supporting growth.
geo_synthesis.json.key_tension: Energy-driven inflation spike forces Fed to abandon dovish pivot just as growth concerns mount from sustained high rates and geopolitical uncertainty.

bull_case.scenario: Swift diplomatic resolution reopens Hormuz, oil crashes back toward $60, Fed pivots dovish on disinflationary relief
bull_case.trigger: Brent crude falling below $90/barrel on ceasefire headlines or alternative supply routes secured

bear_case.scenario: Conflict escalates to broader regional war, oil hits $150+, stagflation deepens as Fed forced to hike into recession
bear_case.trigger: Iran attacks Saudi facilities or US forces, or China moves on Taiwan during Middle East distraction

geo_synthesis.json.prudent_strategy: Overweight energy and hard assets as geopolitical premium likely persists regardless of near-term headlines. Underweight duration risk given Fed's inflation constraints. Quality over growth given margin pressure from energy costs.
